recorded: Both originals ran unchanged, the JavaScript version with Node.js 26.12.1 as node trialforge-message-queue-prototype.js and the Python version with Python 3.15.2 as python3 trialforge_message_queue_prototype.py. The prototype takes no input, calls no LLM, and needs nothing beyond the standard library. Its agents sleep for fixed times, so each run takes about 20 seconds and prints the same text every time, since at least 50 ms separate the events that decide each outcome. Everything is compared exactly in either original's wording, with three kinds of freedom. Where the text names the language's own mechanism (Promise.all, Promise.allSettled, and Promise.race against gather() without and with return_exceptions and wait_for, and EventEmitter against Barramento sobre asyncio in the title), any name is accepted. Records are accepted in Node.js's util.inspect layout, Python's repr, or JSON, with camelCase or snake_case keys in the original order, and booleans in either case. The timeout is accepted as 675ms or 0.675s. Both originals write nothing to standard error.

cases.name: checks itself, then runs the happy path, loses the CSR result when the parallel join fails fast, keeps it and retries the ICF once into the same document when the join waits for both, regenerates only the CSR that finished after the ethics amendment, recovers an ICF that hung past its timeout on the first retry, and gives up after three retries of a persistent hang
